dash.radar.title: How radar sees water, and what it cannot see
dash.radar.p1: Radar sends its own signal and listens for the echo. It works through cloud, rain and darkness.
dash.radar.p2: Calm, open water acts like a mirror. It sends little signal back to the satellite, so it usually looks dark.
dash.radar.p3: Wind can roughen water. Rough water sends more signal back, so it can look bright instead.
dash.radar.p4: NISAR uses L-band, a long wavelength that can pass through some leaves. It may still miss water under thick crops.
dash.radar.p5: Water among tall crops or buildings can look bright, not dark. Radar may miss some of it.
dash.radar.p6: Dark patches can also be other smooth surfaces, such as dry sand or tarmac. They are not always flood.
dash.radar.p7: Radar cannot tell how deep water was, how long it stayed, or what it damaged.
dash.radar.p8: So we say "probably". Nobody has yet checked these results on the ground.

dash.about.title: About and sources
dash.about.intro: Radar data come from the NISAR mission. Alerts and storm facts come from the official sources below. Links open the agency pages. Built by team SpaceBros for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Not an official NASA, ISRO, IMD or government product, and not a warning service.
dash.about.s1.name: NASA/JPL-Caltech and ISRO NISAR, via ASF DAAC and NASA Earthdata
dash.about.s1.what: Source of the L-band radar scenes used here (NISAR L2 GCOV). Scenes are found with the NASA CMR search API and the ASF search API, and the files are read from ASF DAAC with an Earthdata login.
dash.about.s2.name: NASA Earthdata
dash.about.s2.what: Account and archive portal for NISAR data.
dash.about.s3.name: NISAR mission site (NASA/JPL-Caltech)
dash.about.s4.name: NISAR Data User Guide
dash.about.s4.what: Background reading from the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) on how NISAR files are laid out. Not a data source.
dash.about.s5.name: NISAR StoryMaps
dash.about.s5.what: Background reading only. Not used to make any map or number on this page.
dash.about.s6.name: NISAR Applications White Papers
dash.about.s6.what: Background reading only. Not used to make any map or number on this page.
dash.about.s7.name: NASA ARSET: Introduction to SAR
dash.about.s7.what: Background training on how synthetic aperture radar works. Not used to make any map or number on this page.
dash.about.s8.name: GDACS
dash.about.s8.what: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System: cyclone alerts (EC JRC and UN OCHA).
dash.about.s9.name: NDMA SACHET
dash.about.s9.what: India's national alert feed, including state disaster authority alerts.
dash.about.s10.name: IMD
dash.about.s10.what: India Meteorological Department: storm category, wind and landfall details.
dash.about.s11.name: geoBoundaries
dash.about.s11.what: Mandal outlines (ADM3, boundary year 2018, ODbL 1.0). District names for the mandals are from the 2022 Andhra Pradesh district lists.
dash.about.s12.name: Esri basemap
dash.about.s12.what: Map data: Esri, HERE, Garmin, OpenStreetMap contributors.
dash.about.notused: ASF Vertex was not used; scenes were found with the NASA CMR and ASF search APIs. CSA RCM and RADARSAT-1, and CONAE SAOCOM, were not fetched for this pilot. NISAR L-band covers the study area (team to confirm). ISRO S-band scenes are not processed yet.
